exercises.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.muscle_targeting_notes: A horizontal pull emphasizes the mid-back retractors while the lats and elbow flexors assist.
instructions: Set a stable stance or chest support, hinge only as required, and let the shoulder blades reach forward without rounding the lower back.
Draw the elbows toward the torso or the intended path, briefly squeeze the shoulder blades without shrugging, then reach forward slowly.
Breathe steadily through each repetition and keep the range pain-free.
Finish the set when posture or controlled movement begins to change.
common_mistakes: Using momentum or an uncontrolled stretch to move the resistance.
Shrugging or letting the shoulders roll forward instead of controlling the shoulder blades.
Rounding or overextending the lower back under load.
Using a range or resistance that causes pain or prevents steady breathing.
safety_cautions: Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, unusual shortness of breath, or dizziness.
Keep the load close during hinges and stop the set when you cannot maintain a controlled trunk position.
Inspect bars, benches, cables, bands, and anchors before use; use a stable setup and appropriate safeties.
People with a current injury or relevant medical condition should follow advice from a qualified clinician.

exercises.name: Rack Pull
exercises.muscle_targeting_notes: The hinge or trunk-extension pattern loads the spinal erectors and posterior chain; maintain a controlled, neutral spine.
instructions: Set feet about hip width, brace the trunk, and hinge at the hips with a neutral spine; keep the load close to the body.
Draw the elbows toward the torso or the intended path, briefly squeeze the shoulder blades without shrugging, then reach forward slowly.
Breathe steadily through each repetition and keep the range pain-free.
Finish the set when posture or controlled movement begins to change.
common_mistakes: Using momentum or an uncontrolled stretch to move the resistance.
Shrugging or letting the shoulders roll forward instead of controlling the shoulder blades.
Rounding or overextending the lower back under load.
Using a range or resistance that causes pain or prevents steady breathing.
safety_cautions: Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, unusual shortness of breath, or dizziness.
Keep the load close during hinges and stop the set when you cannot maintain a controlled trunk position.
Inspect bars, benches, cables, bands, and anchors before use; use a stable setup and appropriate safeties.
People with a current injury or relevant medical condition should follow advice from a qualified clinician.

exercises.name: Seated Resistance-Band Row
exercises.muscle_targeting_notes: A horizontal pull emphasizes the mid-back retractors while the lats and elbow flexors assist.
instructions: Set a stable stance or chest support, hinge only as required, and let the shoulder blades reach forward without rounding the lower back.
Draw the elbows toward the torso or the intended path, briefly squeeze the shoulder blades without shrugging, then reach forward slowly.
Breathe steadily through each repetition and keep the range pain-free.
Finish the set when posture or controlled movement begins to change.
common_mistakes: Using momentum or an uncontrolled stretch to move the resistance.
Shrugging or letting the shoulders roll forward instead of controlling the shoulder blades.
Rounding or overextending the lower back under load.
Using a range or resistance that causes pain or prevents steady breathing.
safety_cautions: Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, unusual shortness of breath, or dizziness.
Keep the load close during hinges and stop the set when you cannot maintain a controlled trunk position.
Inspect bars, benches, cables, bands, and anchors before use; use a stable setup and appropriate safeties.
People with a current injury or relevant medical condition should follow advice from a qualified clinician.
